Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/02/2026
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8266713
Permit API: 125-29255
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/02/2026
Comments: On March 2, 2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill at the Marchezak John well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Accompanying the Department during this inspection are Range Resources representatives Denny Furmanek and Kevin Rudd. According to the spill report, approximately 25 gallons of diesel fuel were released to the surface of the well pad on February 28, 2026, at 9:30 PM.Prior to starting this inspection, the Department spoke via phone with Range Resources representative Derek Zofchak, who explained that the release occurred when a fuel truck experienced a fuel line failure while filling an on-site storage tank. Zofchak reported that remediation was completed on the day the release occurred, and that impacted material was placed in a rolloff dumpster on site.An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on 11/20/2017.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Containment plan, and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are on site in the mailbox (photos 3-6). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Setup of on-site secondary containment is not yet complete. However, Furmanek had the Containment inspection log available during this inspection (photo 15). The drill permits are on site in the company trailer (photo 16).The location where the 2/28/2026 diesel spill occurred appears to be freshly backfilled with stone (photo 7). No evidence of spilled diesel fuel, such as staining, odor, or a rainbow sheen was observed in this location. The fuel storage tank is placed within secondary containment (photo 8). A rolloff box is on site which reportedly contains the impacted material (photo 13). Rudd and Furmanek explained that air drilling operations have been completed. Drilling operations are expected to continue on the day of this inspection (photo 14). Four gas wells are planned to be drilled during this project. Five gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production. The GPU units and Dehy unit are not equipped with secondary containment (photos 9 and 10). However, the producing wells on site were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 12). All other storage containers and machinery on site that appear to contain regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photo 11). The secondary containments on site appear to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no observable holes or tears.The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 14). Furmanek explained that the well pad was expanded adjacent to the production tanks to better accommodate vehicle traffic for drilling and stimulation operation (photo 13). This location will be assessed in a future inspection, as further review is needed.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be noted and immediately corrected against the 2/28/2026 diesel fuel release.Transmittal of this inspection report was delayed due to an IT Error.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 7/24/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8195551
Permit API: 015-22684
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Herrick Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/24/2024
Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There are two post-construction stormwater management structures onsite. They appear to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 192.8-262 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine gas processing units (GPUs) held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine wells capable of producing. There were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.

Comments: On January 3, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3435475 where violations were outstanding due to a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans, and no NOV response received from the operator. Also, no production reports had been submitted since 2014 per Department database, at the time of that inspection.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photo 1). No Emergency Response plans, or other required documents were onsite. No evidence of leaks or discharge could be found around the new production tanks, and they appeared to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they were not equipped with secondary containment (see photos 3 and 8). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the earthen berms surrounding these tanks, and at the bases of these tanks (see photos 4-7). The well tag and required operator's information was present on the meter box (see photo 8). The Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite. Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 10). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing.Based on observations from today's inspection, the violations that were continued in IR 3435475 shall remain outstanding, since no changes were made since and no NOV response has been received to date. Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8159310
Permit API: 081-21855
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.

These tests are being performed in response to a gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. SPBUTs were initiated on 5/26/20 @ ~ 08:15 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in w/ Frac valves installed on top of well heads. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Craig Shores and Trey Sites, Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andy Sallaway and D.E.P. OGIS, Ken Kennedy. Starting at approx. 10:15, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the HUNTER Pad wells. - HUNTER 5H: (20x13): 3.0 psi.; 68 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:17 ** (13x9): 277 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:23 ** (9x5): 327 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected at 10:27 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:20. - HUNTER 6H: (20x13): 17.0 psi.; 65 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:33 ** (13x9): 169.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:37 ** (9x5): 549.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:40 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:40. - HUNTER 22HC: (20x13): 24.0 psi.; 91 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:45 ** (13x9): 226.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:49 ** (9x5): 396.0 psi.; 92 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:52 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:50. - HUNTER 21HC: (20x13): 44.0 psi.; 93 % CH4; Sampled collected @ 10:55 ** (13x9): 268.0 psi.; 90 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:00 ** (9x5): 131.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:07 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:00. - HUNTER 23HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0 % CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 255.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:13 (9x5): 321.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:20 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:30. - All (5) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to poly tank @ 11:45. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (20x13) and the(13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the HUNTER 23HC (20x13) annulus. This is indicative of defective cement. Since the presence of gas was detected in the HUNTER 5H well (20x13) annulus was not addressed in previous responses received, the Dept. requests in writing, by 7/4/20, how CALLC plans to address this defective condition.

Violation ID: 854473
Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-26
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was on a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed 10-15 feet in the ditch along the access road until it reached the culvert pipe under the access road, it then flowed through the culvert pipe under the road and continued to 300-400 feet through vegetation down grade from the tank battery. A backhoe was brought in at some point after the oil release and a ditch was dug approximately 70-80 feet down grade of the tank battery to contain the oil release. A second ditch was dug approximately 275 feet north and down grade of the first ditch to contain the oil flow already beyond the first ditch. Absorbent pads and loose absorbents were used to collect oil from the atop the water collected in the ditches. The second ditch/trap was set up with drains to allow water to siphon off leaving the oil in containment. Some oil residue was found on the vegetation east of the lower ditch in a connected depression and in the vegetation 10-20 feet north of the ditch/trap. There was no evidence of oil residue beyond these two areas. The oil and water remaining in the secondary containment was removed by a vacuum tanker truck via the discharge pipe, the remaining oil was removed from the leaking tank as well as from the the other tanks on site on Friday, June 21. There were several precipitation events after the oil was released to ground, one on Friday June 21st, the day of the event, another on Monday June 24, the runoff from these events carried the oil down grade to the above mentioned areas. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 550-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil &Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8263955
Permit API: 129-29235
Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On February 4, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Aphrodite Well Site (ESCGP issued on 5/9/2020, amended on 2/5/2024, expiring on 2/4/2029) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 2/3/2026 (CTS 394941). Present during the inspection was operator representative Jim Noon.According to Mr.Noon, this release is a seperate release, unrelated to the release documented in inspection report 4125373.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 5 total wells on the well pad. According to the operator, stimulation for all 5 wells has been completed and they are continuing to install production equipment in order to get the wells into active production.During the inspection, Mr. Noon guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Noon the release was discovered on 2/3/2026 when containment for drilling/stimulation equipment was being removed from the site. He stated that upon removal of the containment, staining was observed and after further assessment it was identified as a release of impaired water and reported to the Department. At the time of the inspection the operator is unsure of the total volume of impaired water that was released.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the release and ongoing remediation was in an approximate 40-foot by 80-foot area adjacent to the well heads near the entrance of the well pad.Mr. Noon stated that 2 small temporary sumps were excavated in the area of the release in order to isolate the release. The water collected in the sumps were being pumped out by a vacuum truck. Mr. Noon stated that 2 roll-off boxes had already been filled with impacted material, and they were waiting for additional boxes to continue remediation.Conductivity readings of 18.08mS, and 6.13mS were obtained in the 2 excavated sumps. Conductivity readings of 3.97mS, 1.25mS, 1.17mS, and 0.69mS were obtained in the area of the release/remediation.The Department requests the operator provide a copy of the secondary containment inspection records from January 1, 2026, through the date the secondary containment was removed, within 3 days of receiving this inspection report.The operator is also requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.If the quantity of the spill is determined to be greater than 1 barrel (42 gallons),the operator will need to perform remediation in accordance with the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Aphrodite 2M well for the observed release. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of the requested information/documentation.

Comments: This administrative inspection documents the receipt of sample results for samples taken on the pad on 4/17/19 and samples taken in the sediment ditch (background and where fluid from the pad entered) and sediment trap outfall taken on 4/18/19. The sample from the pad (ID #0939078) shows elevated levels of barium and strontium, and while the chloride result was cancelled, these elevated parameters show that the high conductance fluid on the pad was likely a release produced water or flowback. The elevated chlorides, barium, and strontium in sample ID #0939080 (as compared to background, represented by sample ID #0939079) show that the fluid migrated from the pad, into the ditch, and into the sediment trap. Alldocumentation regarding the Act 2 clean-up of this site should be submitted to the Department as soon as it is available.The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The original violations regarding the spill at the site have been superseded by the administrative order.Since the most recent inspection of this site on 2/21/2024 (Inspection Record # 3715744) there have been no changes at thesite. All outstanding violations for failure to report production information, failure to comply with the court order, and for failure to plug the well upon abandonment remain unresolved.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 3/26/2026
Comments: On March 26, 2026, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident site inspection at the EQT ARO LLC COP Tract 343 Pad C. On March 25, 2026, at 1526, EQT reported a spill of drilling mud outside of containment onto the well pad surface to the DEP spill hotline. Coastal Rig 103 is onsite conducting plugging operations on the C1015H Well. The plugging rig had moved onsite on Monday, March 23, 2026. Prior to the plugging rig being onsite a snubbing rig was located onsite. When the plugging rig mobilized to the site, large water puddles from recent rain covered some of the well pad. Once the puddles dried, an area approximately 40 feet by 20 feet was noticed to the north of the rig containment. DEP spoke with Tobias Excavating and he said that last evening he tested the impacted area with a PID meter and did not return elevated results on the meter. Tobias said Matt Locke with Tuscarora Geologic and Environmental Services screened the area last evening with a conductivity meter and did not return elevated results on the meter. DEP spoke with EQT Rick Hall on the phone while onsite and EQT thinks drilling mud was sprayed while the snubbing rig was onsite and the spill did not reveal itself until the water onsite dried up. Mr. Hall estimates approximately 25 gallons of drilling mud was spilled outside of containment onto the well pad surface. At the time of inspection, Tobias had already scraped up the impacted area and placed the impacted soil into rolloff dumpsters. Approximately, an inch to three inches of stone and soil were scraped up to remove the impacted material. While conducting the inspection, Tobias was spreading top stone on the area that was scraped up. The spilling of drilling mud outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Due to the immediate response to clean up the spill the violations are consider to be immediately corrected.

Comments: On 4/13/2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection at the Holchin 2 well plugging site in North Union Township, Fayette County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, which was submitted by the operator on 3/16/2026. Tyler Hinkle (Next Level Energy) was on site during this inspection. The following was observed during the inspection:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Next Level Energy representative Tyler Hinkle, who was on site to make minor repairs to the temporary BMPs installed on site and to remove an excavator from site. Hinkle identified during this inspection evidence of third-party disturbance due to livestock grazing on site. The Department recommends that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. Temporary Erosion and sedimentation controls are installed downslope of the access road and well site. No evidence of accelerated erosion was observed on site during this inspection. The site E and S/Restoration plans are available in a mailbox on site. The site appears to be staged for well plugging operations, however no machinery related to well plugging is on site at the time of inspection. The gas well is disconnected from the production equipment. No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site during this inspection. The API number was not visible anywhere on site. While on site, the Department reviewed the site E and S/Restoration plans. The Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is not installed in the location shown in the E and S plan drawing (photos 4 and 15). Although an overall BMP layout drawing exists, the plans state that E and S controls are to be installed at contractor's discretion. At the time of this inspection, the E and S controls appear to be installed on site in a manner that is preventing accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring. The Department recommends that that the operator monitor the site and install additional temporary E and S controls as necessary in order to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to occur. The Department recommends that the site E and S/Restoration plans are kept updated via redlining with the BMP's currently installed on site. Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to failure to follow the E and S plan.An additional violation shall be issued in IR 4177612 for failure to post the API number on site.

Comments: On March 23, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Sanns Frank well site. The inspection is separated into 3 inspection reports due to number of photos. This is inspection 1 of 3.The ESCGP (ESG076322011-00) for this site was issued on 8/27/2021 and was set to expire on 8/26/2026, but was terminated on 11/6/2024 (IRs 3862784 and 3863032).There are 8 total wells on-site at this time. The 1H, 2H, 3H, and 7H appear to be completed and equipped for production at this time. The 4H, 5H, 6H, and 8H appear to have recently completed drilling activities and are currently not in production.Act 9 sign is present and complies with 78a55 fabrication requirements. Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, and ESCGP plans are all present on site. The ERP and PPC plans include the required components.Wet Pond (Photos 4-5) appears to be functioning properly, no E and S issues observed at this time.The area below the outlet and level spreader of MRC Rain Garden #2 (Photos 8-17) appears to be heavily saturated with lack of vegetation and exposed earth as the water flows towards UNT to Mingo Creek. The water appears to be exiting the level spreader in sheet flow, but appears to be channelizing as it exits the LOD into the tree line. At this time, the water is entering the stream but no active sediment discharge is observed.The access road crossing of UNT to Mingo Creek (Photos 22-25) is observed with CFS installed on both sides of the access road. The CFS appears to have been installed properly but appears to have not been maintained and is failing, allowing mud to exit the access road via undercutting. The mud is observed to continuing down the slope below the access road into a pond of water on the East side, which also continues via channelized flow into UNT to Mingo Creek. What appears to be dust from the access road is also observed on the surface below the access road on the East side and is observed on most of the leaf cover in this area. At this time, no active sediment discharge is observed into the stream.On the West side, it appears that the extent of the dust and mud ends within the rip rap, however some gravel is observed off the access road.The rock apron below Channel 8 and the level spreader below MRC Rain Garden #3 both appear to be discharging stormwater in sheet flow, however the vegetation below both features is heavily saturated and the stormwater appears to be channelizing closer to the tree line, where it eventually reaches UNT to Mingo Creek. This area also appears to be impacted by a two track trail. At this time, no active sediment discharge is observed into the stream.Additional vegetation disturbances are observed along the access road (Photos 7-9, 13). No E and S issues are observed in these areas at this time. The DEP recommends the operator stabilize these areas.A small release of what appears to be a petroleum-based fluid is observed on the access road near the mailbox (Photos 18-19). The DEP spoke to Scott Clark (Range Resources) during discovery of the release. Clark appeared to be leaving the well pad and informed the DEP that he was unaware of the release, but would have personnel clean it up today.The DEP recommends the operator properly dispose of the impacted material and requests the disposal documents when made available. No violation is being issued for the release at this time due to the volume of the release appearing to be below reporting limits.Well equipment on the well pad appears to be contained within secondary containment and no other spills, leaks, or releases were observed on the well pad at this time.Wooden stakes with ribbons attached are observed at several disturbed areas on-site and near UNT to Mingo. The DEP requests additional information in regard to the stakes.Violations for accelerated erosion and sedimentation, failed E and S BMPs, and failure to maintain PCSM BMP are being issued at this time.

Comments: On June 4, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline and Justin Abbott conducted a follow up inspection at Beech Resources Premier Pad. This inspection was to follow up with the reported spill from June 2, 2020 and an inspection completed by DEP staff on June 3, 2020. The inspection on June 3, 2020 reported an area of high conductivity still remaining in the impacted area. Don Stevenson with Beech Resources and Matt Tunsing with Penn E&R were onsite. Conductivity of the excavated area of impact was screened and 1 or 2 small depressions were noticed that had a reading of 1 mS/cm to 2.5 mS/cm. The normal levels of conductivity were noted outside and downgrade of the previously delineated area of impact. So the area of impact had not changed from previous delineation. Another area was of high conductivity was noted from the inspection on June 3, 2020. That area was at the edge of the permitted MASS onsite where some off loading had taken place. That area had a small puddle of water about 3 ft. long by 2 ft. wide that was screened for conductivity. The conductivity of the water was about 7 mS/cm and the soil around the puddle was 5 mS/cm. Judging from the area that was screened for conductivity the spill appeared to be less than 5 gallons. Beech Resources said that they would collect the water from the puddle and scrape up the impact soil in that area. No new violations noted. Outstanding violations from Inspection No. 3001824 and Inspection No. 30309142 still remain.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/29/2026
Comments: On January 29, 2026, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection at Range Resources Shearer Robert tank pad located in Robinson Township, Washington County following a spill that was reported to the DEP on 1/27/2026. Accompanying during today's inspection was Range Resources representative Nate Smiell.Documented in IR 4131333, according to the spill report and the phone conversation with Mr. Zofchak, at approximately 2:55 AM on January 27, 2026 a water truck was staged on the tank pad when a closed valve on the back of the truck began leaking into a bleeder valve hose, subsequently releasing Produced Water onto the gravel pad in an approximately 20 ft by 100 ft area. Water truck drivers contained the release to the graveledwell pad and began vacuuming up the pooled fluid, SPSI arrived on site on 1/27/2026 and began scraping the gravel tank pad. The release was estimated to be approximately 193 gallons, and no waters of the Commonwealth were reportedly impacted.At the time of this inspection, an Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it and in the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan, and a Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Smiell showed the Department the approximate location of the incident area and stated that SPSI finished scraping the tank pad and filled 2 roll off dumpsters with contaminated gravel on 1/27/2026. The area which appeared to be approximately 100 ft by 20 ft was observed to be recently scraped. Some spray paint was observed on the gravel to mark the areas where Mr. Smiell reported that samples were collected on 1/28/2026 in accordance with Act 2 requirements. Soil conductivity readings could not be collected due to the ground being frozen, however, the Department did not observe any visible evidence of Produced Water remaining on the graveled tank pad. Range is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, and plan for remediation of the violations. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled.Range will need to follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Range will also need to assess the impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the release.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the 193 gallon release of Produced Water onto the graveled tank pad.

Inspection Date: 6/04/2026
Comments: On 06/03/2026 at 0017 hours the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) received a notification of a release at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County (CTS #398207). Representative Ralph Babcock stated "on 6/2/26 at 5:15 p.m., a Keystone Clear Water truck driver was loading production water when the line split releasing 25 gallons of produced water. Approximately 10 gallons of produced water spilled into a containment structure while the remaining 15 gallons of produced water spilled onto the ground. Keystone Clearwater vacuumed produced water from the containment structure and scraped up impacted soil for later disposal.The DEP contacted Repsol and spoke with Mr. Babcock at 1145 hours. He stated the material from the release had been recovered and placed in drums onsite. He stated the release took place in the off-loading area of the pad. He stated he was notified of the released at 2345 hours (06/02).On 06/04/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection. I arrived at 0915 hours and met with Mr. Babcock. Environmental Resources was onsite to collect samples from the release and the prior release (CTS#396090). The area of the release was ~33 feet long (photo #2). There were no pooled fluids in the area of the release. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 452-1042 us/cm. The cause of the release was due to a valve malfunction (photo #3). Environmental resources screened the soil in the area of the release and received readings of 1-1.3 mS/cm (1000-1300 us/cm). The recovered material was observed in drums onsite and held within secondary containment (photo #4).The DEP screened the area of the prior release (CTS #396090). Fluids within the stormwater ditch at the release point were field measured for EC at ~452 us/cm. Mr. Babcock stated that this week there would be more material removed from the stormwater ditch at the release point due to elevated soil readings. There was dead vegetation observed downgrade of the affected bio-retention basin (photo #15-16). Fluids within and directly upgrade of the furthest downgrade sump pump were measured for EC between 1.248-2.24 mS/cm (1248-2240 us/cm) (photo #17 and 18). Fluids downgrade of the sump pump were field measured for EC between 173.7-398 us/cm. The violations related to the recent spill (CTS #398207) are considered immediately corrected however, outstanding violations remain open for API#015-23994 from the previous release (CTS #396090).I departed at 1120 hours.

Comments: The Department was made aware on Tuesday, July 21, 2020 by an adjacent unconventional well operator of a communication incident impacting two offset unconventional wells operated by the adjacent operator. The adjacent operator reported two active producing wells, permit numbers 125-26943 and 125-26945, received a measurable transfer of fluid and pressure from the CNX Gas LLC, RHL28-GHSM (API 059-27830), an offset unconventional well currently undergoing hydraulic fracturing. According to the adjacent offset operator, observations of fluid and pressure were observed at the two wells beginning on or around on July 15, 2020. According to the adjacent offset operator, unconventional wells 125-26943 and 125-26945, are within the zone of influence of the RHL28-GHSM (API 059-27830) unconventional well currently undergoing hydraulic fracturing. The adjacent operator reported to the Department that CNX Gas LLC, was notified on July 20, 2020 of the communication incident by the adjacent operator. The Department previously received an electronic notification from CNX Gas LLC, that stimulation activities would begin on the RHL28-GHSM on Thursday, July 9, 2020 at 6:00 pm. The Department contacted CNX Gas LLC, on Tuesday July 21, 2020 regarding the communication incident. The Department informed CNX Gas LLC, of the notification and reporting requirements required by 78a.73(c). CNX Gas LLC, personnel indicated they are aware of the communication incident and are coordinating with the adjacent operator. To date, the Department has not received an electronic notification of the well communication incident in accordance with 78a.73(c).The Department reviewed the Area of Review (AOR) report deliverables as required by 78a.52a(c) and the as-drilled well plats and well records for the RHL28-GHSM (API 059-27830). According to the as drilled plats, 125-26943 and 125-26945 are within the AOR zone of influence of the RHL28-GHSM (API 059-27830). The AOR Summary Report information submitted to the Department on August 9, 2019 for the RHL28-GHSM (API 059-27830) failed to identify 125-26943 and 125-26945 as offset unconventional wells located within the zone of influence.After review of all available information, the Department issuing the following violations. See Notice of Violations section below.
